sections.title: Core Security Concepts
sections.content:
CIA triad: Confidentiality (only authorized access), Integrity (data unaltered), Availability (accessible when needed).
AAA: Authentication (who you are), Authorization (what you can do), Accounting (what you did). Enforced via RADIUS or TACACS+ with a central server.
Least privilege and separation of duties limit damage. Defense in depth layers controls.
Zero trust — never trust, always verify; authenticate every request, segment heavily (microsegmentation).
Threat/risk terms: vulnerability (weakness), threat (potential cause), exploit (the attack), risk (likelihood × impact).
Control types: preventive, detective, corrective; and technical, administrative, physical.
exam_tips: AAA = Authentication, Authorization, Accounting (RADIUS/TACACS+ provide it).
Least privilege + defense in depth + zero trust are the recurring design principles.

sections.title: Common Attacks
sections.content:
Know these cold:
DoS/DDoS — overwhelm a target; distributed uses a botnet.
On-path (MITM) — attacker relays/alters traffic between two parties.
ARP spoofing/poisoning — forges ARP replies to redirect LAN traffic (enables MITM).
MAC flooding — overflows the switch MAC table so it floods frames (sniffing).
DNS poisoning/spoofing — corrupts DNS answers to redirect users.
VLAN hopping — reaches other VLANs via double-tagging or switch spoofing.
Rogue DHCP / evil twin AP — impostor services that hijack clients.
Deauthentication — forces Wi-Fi clients off (wireless DoS).
Social engineering — phishing, pretexting, tailgating (attacks the human).
Spoofing — forging source IP/MAC. On-path + spoofing underlie many LAN attacks.
exam_tips: ARP spoofing enables on-path (MITM) attacks on a LAN; mitigate with dynamic ARP inspection.
An 'evil twin' is a rogue AP impersonating a legitimate SSID to capture clients.
MAC flooding overflows the switch table to force frame flooding (sniffing).

concept_cards.hook: The three security goals: Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability.
Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting — centrally provided by RADIUS or TACACS+.
Granting users and systems only the minimum access needed to do their job, limiting the blast radius of compromise.
An attacker secretly relays and may alter communication between two parties, often set up via ARP spoofing.
Forging ARP replies to associate the attacker's MAC with another host's IP, redirecting LAN traffic for interception.
A rogue access point broadcasting a legitimate SSID to trick clients into connecting so traffic can be captured.
An attack that reaches VLANs a port shouldn't, via double-tagging or switch spoofing.
A Distributed Denial-of-Service attack that floods a target from many compromised hosts (a botnet) to exhaust its resources.

practice_questions.q: Which triad defines the core goals of information security?
practice_questions.explanation: The CIA triad — Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability — frames security objectives.

practice_questions.q: Forging ARP replies to intercept LAN traffic is which attack?
practice_questions.explanation: ARP spoofing maps the attacker's MAC to a victim's IP to intercept traffic (enabling on-path).

practice_questions.q: Which protocol provides centralized AAA and is used with 802.1X?
practice_questions.explanation: RADIUS centralizes authentication, authorization, and accounting for network access.

practice_questions.q: An attacker relays and may alter traffic between two parties. This is a(n):
practice_questions.explanation: An on-path/man-in-the-middle attacker sits between endpoints to read or modify traffic.

practice_questions.q: Granting a user only the permissions needed for their job is which principle?
practice_questions.explanation: Least privilege minimizes rights to limit the impact of a compromise.

practice_questions.q: Overflowing a switch's MAC table to force it to flood frames is:
practice_questions.explanation: MAC flooding fills the CAM table so the switch floods frames, enabling sniffing.

practice_questions.q: Splitting a critical task so no single person controls it end-to-end is:
practice_questions.explanation: Separation of duties reduces fraud/error by dividing control of sensitive tasks.

practice_questions.q: A fake access point impersonating a legitimate SSID is a(n):
practice_questions.explanation: An evil twin mimics a trusted SSID to capture client connections and data.

practice_questions.q: Layering multiple independent security controls is called:
practice_questions.explanation: Defense in depth stacks controls so one failure doesn't breach everything.

practice_questions.q: Forged 802.11 frames knocking Wi-Fi clients off the network is a:
practice_questions.explanation: Deauth attacks spoof management frames to disconnect clients (a wireless DoS).
